# dsh-performance-optimizer
DSH bundle that exposes **host-wide and per-event-loop performance metrics** so the user (via a Sett
ings tab) and the agent (via a native tool and a stdio MCP server) can reason about scroll lag, memo
ry drift, and tool loops.
The bundle is intentionally minimal — it samples Node `process.memoryUsage()` / `process.cpuUsage()`
once per second, keeps a 60-sample rolling buffer, and exposes it through three surfaces:
| surface                | consumer                  | mechanism
| Settings → Plugins tab | user                      | `client.js` mounts `<perf-settings-tab>` into

the per-plugin detail page; live table + Canvas2D chart with CPU / RSS / Heap / Wall tabs. |
| Floa
ting HUD           | user (opt-in)             | `client.js` mounts `<perf-hud>` into the document b

ody when `hudVisible: true`.        |
| Native tool            | agent (in-session)        | `ctx.to
ols.register('performance_report')` returns a fresh JSON report on demand.       |
## Files
| file                | role
| `index.js`          | Host half. Owns the sampler, the `performanceOptimizer` Cordis service, and

the `performance_report` tool. |
| `client.js`         | Web GUI half. Two custom elements (`<perf-s
ettings-tab>`, `<perf-hud>`); routes by `ctx.slot`. Calls back into the Host via the runtime bridge.

## What it measures
| sample field | source                                                | what it answers
| `t` / `tHr`  | `Date.now()` + `process.hrtime.bigint()`              | When was this sample taken

(clock / monotonic, never trust the wall for ordering). |
| `rss`        | `process.memoryUsage().rs
s`                           | Has the Host process grown? Did `release`/manual GC help?

|
| `heapUsed`   | `process.memoryUsage().heapUsed`                      | V8 heap pressu

re (RSS includes native).                                          |
| `heapTotal`  | `process.memor
yUsage().heapTotal`                     | Did V8 grow the heap (hint of churn).

|
| `external`   | `process.memoryUsage().external`                      | Na

tive buffers / modules.                                                       |
| `cpuMs`      | `pr
ocess.cpuUsage()`                                  | Cumulative user/system CPU time (ms).

|
| `cpuDeltaMs` | delta against previous sample

| CPU burn between two ticks; correlates with sampler tick & loop work.            |
| `wallDe
ltaMs`| `now - lastCpu.takenAt`                               | Sampler timer drift — catches stalle

d timers caused by event-loop saturation.   |
| `uptimeMs`   | `process.uptime() * 1000`
| Host uptime.                                                                    |
History is the last `historySize` samples (default 60). Sampling interval is `sampleIntervalMs` (def
ault 1000 ms). When MCP is enabled, the most recent report is also written to a JSON file under the
bundle's plugin directory every tick so the stdio MCP server can read it without holding a reference
into the Host process.
## How it talks to DSH
The Host half uses only Cordis accessors declared in `inject`:
- `tools` — registers `performance_report`. Every MCP tool call routed through DSH eventually surfac
es through `tools.register`, so this is the canonical agent interface regardless of whether `@deepse

ek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` is also mounted.
- `pluginContext` — composition helper; lets the patch layer
attach additional reads.
The Client half is mounted once per `dsh.client.inject` target. The `package.json` lists three:
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-plugins` — registers the per-plugin detail tab. This is the c

anonical user surface.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-shell` — registers the HUD.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-cl
ient-ui-conversation` — reserved for a future chip; currently no-op.
It looks up the runtime bridge via `window.__DSH_HOST__` / `window.__DSH__` / `window.deepseek.host`
(whichever is present) and calls `plugin:performance-optimizer.snapshot | .history | .config | .sam
ple | .reset`. If the bridge is missing, the tab renders an empty state and the HUD shows `—` — neit
her blocks the rest of the UI.

## Agent surface
The bundle exposes one native tool:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It returns the same JSON-shaped report shown above. Every MCP tool call routed through DSH ultimatel
y surfaces through `ctx.tools.register`, so this is the canonical agent interface — there is no sepa
rate MCP server in this bundle.
If you want external MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex, an inspector) to also pull snapshots, write a
small sibling DSH plugin that mounts an MCP server and reads `ctx.performanceOptimizer.buildReport()
` for each tool call. Keeping MCP server concerns out of this bundle avoids coupling to a specific `
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` version.
